messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a cascade of reconnects from EU edge yesterday around 03:12 UTC. Clients report rapid reconnect loops and we see a ton of 200+ reconnect events in the billing console :grimacing:
cheng: which proxy pool? any traces?
maya: proxy-pool-eu-2. Logs show an idle-reset right before clients trigger SSE reconnects. Not the normal 30s idle close, this is a sudden RST from the proxy.
ben: that pool had a small kernel update last night — could be TCP keepalive interval changed. ops-bot attached the deploy postmortem.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-tune/2026-03-18 applied to proxy-pool-eu-2 at 02:40 UTC
deploy-bot: Rollout completed to 3/3 hosts in pool eu-2 (canary ok)
sophia: console-team — metrics look weird. The streaming console shows reconnect spikes but sampling for detailed traces is 0 for those sessions. We lost visibility.
console-team: this smells like a sampling edge-case: when a session is torn with RST instead of graceful close, our session-id never flushes and the console sampler skips the trace.
cheng: interesting — sampler relies on closed frames to flush metadata. RST bypasses that. We could wire sampler to flush on socket error too.
ben: but flushing on any socket error may double-report in normal failover cases. We need idempotency.
maya: impact: customers saw doubled token billing for resumed streams + no trace in console to attribute. So it's billing + observability.
sophia: can we annotate reconnects in the console aggregated view even if we don't have full trace? A lightweight marker so SREs can correlate billing spikes.
console-team: yes we can emit a "session_forced_reset" metric from the proxy with tenant_id + short hash. No full trace, just marker. That should preserve PII rules.
cheng: routing policy question: when a proxy idle-reset happens, clients reconnect and get routed to a different shard. That causes KV cache miss and extra model tokens. Could we bias routing during a rollout to prefer sticky leases for 60s after a host reboot?
ben: sticky bias helps but hurts load balancing. For rollouts we could enable a temporary sticky-policy when a host restarts to reduce cold-KV churn. Needs testing.
maya: quick mitigation: revert the kernel-tune on eu-2 and enable probe-ping from proxy -> origin every 10s to detect liveliness without RST.
op-bot: created issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/PROXY-9874 (priority P1)
deploy-bot: proposed rollback queued for pool eu-2 — scheduled immediate canary rollback (confirm with @cheng)
cheng: confirmed, rolling back. But long-term we should fix sampler and console markers, and consider a rollout-only routing policy to reduce cache churn.
sophia: UX note — Console: add a "probable reset" filter to the streaming dashboard and a cost-impact quicklink. Teams asked for a one-click view: spikes -> sample traces -> impacted tenants.
console-team: will prototype an annotation + quicklink. Plan: emit marker, surface in per-route dashboard, add a little toast for cost anomalies.
ben: I'll follow up on sticky rollout policy RFC. Short-term fix timeline: rollback + marker + transient probe.
maya: thanks everyone. After rollback I'll run a small canary of the probe and watch metrics for 30m, then share a repro trace if it recurs.
cheng: also update runbooks: if resets spike, check kernel-tune, check probe status, and manually enable marker if sampler fails.
maya: adding that to the incident playbook now. :thumbsup:
